full_judgment: 25. This Court also notes, that the Court of Settlement as it appears from the impugned Judgment has considered the crucial point as to whether the petitioner has been able to rebut the position taken by the respondent Government that the said Mojibur Rahman Khan was not present in Bangladesh and his whereabouts were not known on 28-2-1972, i.e., the date when PO 16 of 1972 came into force. The petitioner, therefore, at material times during the Settlement Court proceedings was under an obligation to rebut the presumption under section 5(2) of the Ordinance. The Court of Settlement categorically found, upon considering the documentary evidence on record that the petitioner not Only failed to prove that Mojibur Rahman Khan was indeed present in Bangladesh but were far less able to prove that his claim of title to the property in question was immuned from the perilous effect of PO 16 of 1972.
